bull.b: Rapid growth in revenue and ARR demonstrates continued enterprise demand for Zscaler’s recurring cloud security platform. This expanding subscription base supports predictable revenue, creates opportunities for upselling, and provides a durable foundation for sustained growth over the next several quarters.

bull.t: High margins and strong cash generation
bull.b: Strong gross margins and consistently positive free cash flow indicate that Zscaler converts its subscription revenue into substantial internal funding. This supports product investment, sales expansion, and balance-sheet flexibility while operating profitability continues to mature.

bull.t: Broad platform expansion and enterprise adoption
bull.b: Rising adoption among large enterprises and broader deployment across the platform strengthen Zscaler’s competitive position. Larger customers and multi-product usage can improve retention, increase expansion potential, and make the platform more embedded in customers’ security architectures.

bear.b: Persistent GAAP operating and net losses show that Zscaler has not yet fully converted its revenue scale into accounting profitability. Although improving EBITDA is encouraging, continued losses can constrain earnings quality and leave execution dependent on maintaining strong growth and cost discipline.

The lower growth outlook indicates that Zscaler’s expansion rate may decelerate as its revenue base becomes larger. Slower growth could reduce operating leverage and make successful platform expansion, cross-selling, and new AI security offerings increasingly important to sustaining long-term performance.

Higher spending on data-center infrastructure and Zero Trust Branch appliances can absorb more of the cash generated by the subscription business. If elevated investment persists, it may restrain free cash flow conversion and delay the financial benefits of the company’s improving operating profile.
